rule: Spawn point (spawn2): respawn seconds with a variance window of plus or minus half the variance, floor 100 ms. Starts with a respawn roll that fires at once on a fresh zone; a saved remaining time overrides on restart. Gated by a spawn condition value. The group picks one entry by weight among entries that pass a time window, a condition filter and a per-type cap; a group cap is checked first; unique-by-name or over-cap retries in 5 s. On death the point starts its respawn timer and saves the remaining time. Despawn: on its timer a live, unengaged creature is removed; modes 1 and 3 wait the respawn time, modes 2 and 4 the grace time; engaged creatures are kept and rescheduled. Roambox wander: up to 10 tries of a random offset within the box distance, clamped to the box, with ground within 100 units and a path test at heights 0, +250, -250; re-roll if on an edge; then pause for a random time between min and delay. Grid wander: 10 types (circular, random 10 nearest, random, ping-pong patrol, one-way repop, random 5 with line of sight, one-way depop, centre point, random centre, random path). Idle zone: with no clients, creature processing is skipped unless the spawn is flagged or the settle timer runs. Spawn events: a scheduled set or add/subtract/multiply/divide on a spawn condition, with a period in EQ minutes and an optional strict hour. Known defects: random timer returns 14 s when min equals max; variance floor applied after the roll; despawn modes 3 and 4 return before the point's own timer start (not traced end to end).

look_test: Three creatures in a six-tile box on a test zone. Show a fixed two-second pause against a random one-to-three-second pause side by side on a 375-wide phone. Add the defect case with equal minimum and maximum pause to show the 14-second stall. Then a lair gated by a brazier that a timed event lights every fixed period. Dom judges whether the random pause reads as alive, whether the stall reads as broken, and whether the lit brazier reads as a schedule the player can learn.
